## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.markSegment — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt

## Trigger

None — the gap is internal to markSegment's own execution, not a
missing call; nothing external needs to be observed for the fix.

## Today

markSegment declares `Result<Race>` and returns `Result.failure(...)`
for its own checked cases (unknown race id, no current segment). But
inside the RUN-segment branch it calls
`runBlocking { profileRepository.observe().first() }` and then
`CorrectionFactorCalculator.compute`, with no try/catch around either.
`profileRepository.observe()` is backed by `profileDao.observe()`
(Room), so a failure there — a database read error — throws out of the
`runBlocking` block, out of `markSegment`, and past the `Result<Race>`
contract the signature promises. The caller,
`SegmentMarkingController.markSegment`, only calls `.fold(...)` on the
returned `Result` and has no try/catch of its own, so the exception
would propagate further still.

## Expected

markSegment catches any exception raised anywhere in its body —
including the profile read and the correction-factor computation — and
returns it as `Result.failure(...)` instead of letting it escape, so
every failure inside markSegment comes back through its declared
`Result<Race>` contract.

## Searched

markSegment, runBlocking, Result<Race>, RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl, profileRepository.observe
